value.a: FOUR, and the first is asked to be ratified rather than merely recorded. (1) A PROVED NODE'S FALSIFIER MAY BE RE-SPELLED BY A LATER NODE WITHOUT BEING RETRACTED, provided the later node's own falsifier carries the earlier substance forward explicitly. an-inference-call-logs-that-it-started proved on 2026-08-18 naming diagnostics.jsonl by name and matching trail-to-meter by canonical TEXT; both spellings change here, its record is not edited (Law 7), and clause (5) of this falsifier is where its substance is carried. Without such a rule the corpus either freezes at its first spelling or a proof quietly stops meaning what it proved. I could not find this written anywhere. (2) BUILD-MINIMAL DEFERS THE POLICY; THE CHECK IT DOES NOT PERFORM IS WHETHER THE SHAPE CAN STILL HOLD THE POLICY LATER. This is the general form of the 'WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT' miss, and it is a real addition to build-minimal rather than a criticism of it: deferring rotation was right, and the grain that made rotation inexpressible was chosen in the same breath with nothing asking the question. (3) FILE-PER-EMISSION IS MORE APPEND-ONLY, NOT LESS. It reads like a conflict with breadcrumb_log.py's 'PURE APPEND, ON PURPOSE, AGAINST BOTH PRECEDENTS' and is the opposite: a written file is never reopened at all, where an appended trail is reopened by every later write. (4) A SHAPE THAT CANNOT EXPRESS EXPIRY IS NOT THE SAME AS A SHAPE THAT HAS NOT CHOSEN AN EXPIRY. Easy to lose, and losing it is how the deferral in (2) became invisible.
